Use the listed grammar and structures actively and accurately.
Know the Hebrew letters and consonants.
Use vowel-letters.
Know the vowels (not vocalisation).
Apply accent and pronunciation patterns.
Know morphology of nouns and verbs.
Identify masculine and feminine nouns by endings such as -ah and -t.
Recognise nouns feminine by nature, body parts, countries and cities.
Recognise extraordinary nouns and those used in both genders.
Form the dual with -ayim for time, numbers, paired body parts, clothes and tools.
Recognise -ayim nouns that are not dual.
Form regular plurals in -im and -ot.
Recognise extraordinary plurals.
Decline nouns that do not change, or that change their vowels, with possessive suffixes.
Decline segolite nouns.
Form the construct state with unchanged and changed first parts.
Form construct plurals and changes of internal vocalisation.
Know three-root and four-root verbs, tenses and forms.
Use active qal, pi'el, hif'il, passive nif'al, pu'al, hof'al and reflexive hitpa'el.
Use the imperative, infinitive, verbal noun and participles.
Conjugate the sound verb in all forms.
Conjugate common verbs and irregular verbs.
Use common adjectives and colours.
Use positive, comparative and superlative forms.
Use common adverbs.
Use personal, possessive, demonstrative and relative pronouns and pronominal suffixes.
Use the article ha with nouns and adjectives.
Use prepositions b, k, l, m, el, al, im, min and the combined forms with their functions.
Use conjunctions such as v, gam, ela, az, afilu.
Form interrogatives such as mah, mi, matai, lamah, eich.
Express condition with im, lu, ilu.
Negate with lo, ein, adayin lo, terem and the negative imperative.
Express result with lachen, mishum kach, biglal zeh.
Express contrast with aval, ulam, bechol zot, lamrot.
Use the indefinites mishehu and mashehu.
Use interjections such as Hallo, Oy, nu.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers and days of the week.
Identify subject, verb, predicate, objects, attribute and adverbs.
Build simple, compound and complex sentences.
Order subject, verb, predicate, adverbs, nouns and adjectives correctly.
Use intonation to mark statements versus questions, and repetition for emphasis.
Recognise fixed noun patterns that signal professions, colours, illnesses, places and tools.
Recognise fixed verb patterns for passive, reflexive, reciprocal and causative meaning.
Use the infinitive as object, for purpose, and after wish, ability and need words.
Express possession and lack with yesh and ein.
Distinguish complete from incomplete sentences.
Use plural after 'all' or 'most', and linking words such as aval, ach, ela, afilu.
Vary word order for emphasis, place gam correctly and turn simple into compound sentences.
Study one text and one film, or two texts.
Choose from set works.
Study a set text: Oz's Don't call it night, Liebrecht's Horses on the Highway or at least 10 Amichai poems.
Study a set film: The Summer of Aviya or Someone to Run With.
Respond critically in Modern Hebrew to concepts, issues and form.
Choose one research topic and cover all its points.
Research equality: gender equality, non-Jewish minorities and Jewish ethnic minorities.
Research war and conflict: history of the wars, their effect on society and the army's role.
Research Israeli music: changing sound, contemporary musicians and influence on young people.
Research peace movements: the pursuit of peace, international bodies and a peaceful future.
